clue.text: Fizzy drink small, easy to reach

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
something handy is close by and easy to get at

explanation.surface: A little fizzy drink kept within easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: SHANDY is beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer, a British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a beer-and-lemonade mix, so it is a sparkling beverage.

clue.text: Charlie's vacuum cleaner?

definitions.meaning: British slang: a charlie is a fool; the 's is short for is
humorously, a vacuum cleaner is something that sucks

explanation.surface: A household appliance belonging to someone called Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' is British slang for a gullible fool, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker is a dupe, an easily fooled person, and also literally anything that sucks.

clue.text: Naval chief revised chart to include variable London landmark

parts.note: an admiral is a top naval officer

indicators.note: to include means to hold within, so the variable goes inside the rearranged letters
revised means altered, so the letters of chart are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer redraws a map to add an uncertain London site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns CHART into TARCH; 'to include' puts Y inside it. Admiralty Arch is a ceremonial gateway off Trafalgar Square in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Admiralty Arch is a well-known monumental gateway building in central London.

clue.text: Outline you need help to lift weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word for help reads it bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: You need assistance to raise something heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' reverses AID to DIA in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagram is a simple drawn plan showing the shape or structure of something.

clue.text: Just pants put on line

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece put on another comes after it, so the word for pants follows the line letter

parts.note: British slang: 'pants' means rubbish, awful

explanation.surface: Underwear hung on a washing line, said to be fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear but is British slang for something poor or awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and legal, in keeping with the law.

clue.text: Legendary musketeer in combat, hostile

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A famous swordsman fighting fiercely in battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the name across 'combAT HOStile'.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is one of Dumas's three musketeers, alongside Porthos and Aramis.

clue.text: Well suited to the job, athletic pro scrambled up ropes

parts.note: athletic means fit
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so the letters of up ropes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sporty professional climbs ropes, perfect for the task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' looks like the verb climbed; it rearranges UP ROPES into PURPOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit for purpose is an idiom for good enough to do what is needed.

clue.text: One's fixed on banger maybe left on dish

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: A sausage left on a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a sausage but is British slang for an old car; an L-plate is the red L sign on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Learner drivers must display an L-plate on their vehicle, often a cheap old car.

clue.text: Commander Mike to hand over navigational device

parts.note: CO is commanding officer, a commander
Mike is the NATO alphabet word for M
to pass something is to hand it over

explanation.surface: A military commander tells Mike to give him the navigation instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A compass shows direction, the basic instrument for finding one's way.

clue.text: Son called during trial — most odd

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so these letters go inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A son phoned in the middle of a court case, which was very peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the insertion signal; 'trial' suggests a court case but is simply a test.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangest is the superlative of strange, meaning the oddest.

clue.text: Heated the Spanish accommodation

parts.note: heated means hot
EL is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Warm lodgings in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is a building offering paid lodging, a kind of accommodation.

clue.text: Temperature having dropped, fear slip

indicators.note: with the temperature letter dropped, it is taken out of the word for fear

parts.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: As the temperature falls, someone slips in fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dropped' removes T from TERROR.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, which is an error.

clue.text: Again photograph changing shore at first over time

indicators.note: changing tells us to rearrange the letters of the word shore
at first takes only the opening letter of the word over

explanation.surface: A photographer retakes a shot of a shifting coastline once time is up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges SHORE to RESHO; 'at first' takes O from 'over'.
explanation.definitionFit: To reshoot is to film or photograph a scene a second time.

clue.text: Hard sweet idiot let fall

parts.note: British slang: a lemon is a foolish person
to drop is to let fall

explanation.surface: A fool lets a boiled sweet slip from his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemon drop is a lemon-flavoured boiled candy, hard rather than chewy.

clue.text: Desert marathon perhaps an exhausting grind

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
a marathon is one kind of race

explanation.surface: A long run across a desert is a tiring slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sandy terrain but is the verb meaning abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the relentless competitive struggle of working life.

clue.text: Notice minister flipped on key part of speech

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the minister's title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is the short form of Reverend, a minister
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: A notice about a clergyman upset over an important grammatical term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' reverses REV to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb is a word class modifying verbs, such as quickly.

clue.text: Protective wear Rachel half concealed on police force

indicators.note: with half of the name Rachel hidden away, only its back half remains

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Rachel is partly hidden by protective gear worn by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half concealed' drops the first half of RACHEL, leaving HEL; 'on' puts it above MET in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is a hard hat worn to protect the head.

clue.text: Highly esteemed lady longing to probe teacher, English

indicators.note: to probe is to poke into, so the word for longing goes inside the word for teacher

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A desire to investigate an English teacher, a woman of standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to probe' is the insertion signal; a don is a university lecturer at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected senior woman in a field.

clue.text: Only distributed new fabric

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: Just a fresh cloth handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' is the anagram signal, acting on 'Only' alone, with new's letter added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic material woven into cloth for clothing and stockings.

clue.text: Religious class absorbed by the Trinity

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so the class letters sit within the word the

parts.note: the word the, taken as written
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: A divinity lesson spent studying the Holy Trinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' is the insertion signal; Religious Education is a compulsory subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trinity is the Father, Son and Holy Spirit, a group of three.

clue.text: Loner ordered to join army?

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase, matching the verb

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary person is commanded to sign up for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges LONER; the question mark flags army as one example of signing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign on as a member, as recruits do when enlisting.

clue.text: Fly circles minute eatery

parts.note: to fly is to tear along at speed
two circles give two O shapes

explanation.surface: An insect loops around a tiny café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb meaning rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea room is a small café serving tea and light meals.

clue.text: Husband at home in resting place, running late

indicators.note: in places the husband and at-home letters inside the word for resting place

parts.note: a bed is a place to rest
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man at home in bed is running behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' is the insertion signal, while the first 'at home' gives letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind as an adjective means lagging after schedule, which is being late.

clue.text: Building material church folk accept finally

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
folk means people, men

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word accept

explanation.surface: A church congregation eventually agrees on what to build with.
explanation.definitionFit: Cement is the binding powder used in mortar and concrete for construction.
